model_evidence.title: Graph forecast learning curves (supervised forecast errors, not a portfolio)
model_evidence.summary: Twelve preregistered trials trained a neural forecaster of 1-, 5- and 20-session returns three ways: with real correlation edges, with no graph, and with randomly shuffled edges (two seeds, raw and standardized targets, six saved checkpoints). The metric is forecast error on a 64-day 2021 validation window.
model_evidence.verdict: Null result. No trial beat the always-predict-zero control; real correlation edges performed the same as randomly shuffled edges on every horizon and seed, and removing the graph entirely did no worse. Longer training only deepened overfitting. Because the shuffled-edges control failed to separate, the correlation-edge content carries no usable signal here.

model_evidence.title: Table vs graph vs movie representation comparison (supervised forecast errors, not a portfolio)
model_evidence.summary: Eighteen preregistered trials fed byte-identical frozen 2021 information to a table model, a graph model and a 2D “movie” raster (three seeds each, plus shuffled-layout, no-memory and predict-zero controls). The metric is masked next-day return forecast error.
model_evidence.verdict: Null result. No arm beat predicting zero by a meaningful margin; the informative movie layout tied its shuffled-layout control and temporal memory never helped in any paired comparison. These are development-period forecast diagnostics with no costs, taxes or execution.
